questiontext.text: What is the time complexity of recursively copying a binary tree with n nodes?

feedback.text: Correct — each node is visited and cloned exactly once.
No — you must touch every node, not just a root-to-leaf path.
No — there is no per-node logarithmic factor; it is linear.
No — no node is processed more than once.

generalfeedback.text: COPY visits every node once to allocate a clone and recurse on both subtrees, giving O(n).

questiontext.text: Which recursive procedure correctly copies a binary tree?

answer.text: Create a new node with the same value, then recursively copy the left and right subtrees

feedback.text: Correct — clone the node, then recurse on both children.

answer.text: Return the same node reference so both trees share nodes

feedback.text: No — that aliases the original; a true copy allocates new nodes.

answer.text: Copy only the root and leave children NULL

feedback.text: No — a copy must reproduce the entire subtree structure.

answer.text: Copy the left subtree but link the original right subtree

feedback.text: No — both subtrees must be freshly copied.

generalfeedback.text: COPY(t): if t is empty return empty; else make a new node with t's value and set its children to COPY(t.left) and COPY(t.right).

questiontext.text: In the EQUAL algorithm, what should be returned when both trees are empty?

feedback.text: Correct — two empty trees are considered equal.
No — two empty trees match; this is the successful base case.

answer.text: It depends on the depth reached

feedback.text: No — depth is irrelevant; both-empty always means equal.
No — both-empty is a well-defined base case returning true.

generalfeedback.text: Base cases: both empty ⇒ equal; exactly one empty ⇒ not equal; otherwise compare values and recurse.

questiontext.text: In EQUAL, what is returned when exactly one of the two trees is empty?

feedback.text: Correct — one empty and one non-empty cannot match.
No — differing structure here means not equal.
No — the empty side has no value to compare; the answer is not equal.

answer.text: Recurse into the non-empty tree only

feedback.text: No — a structural mismatch is decided immediately as not equal.

generalfeedback.text: If one tree ends before the other, their structures differ, so EQUAL returns false immediately.

questiontext.text: Both the recursive COPY and EQUAL algorithms run in O(n) time on a tree of n nodes.

feedback.text: Correct — each visits every node a constant number of times.
They are — both are linear-time recursive traversals.

questiontext.text: The EQUAL algorithm checks only that two trees have the same shape, ignoring node values.

feedback.text: No — EQUAL requires identical structure AND matching node values.
Correct — EQUAL compares both structure and values.

questiontext.text: COPY and EQUAL naturally finish a node's children before combining their results at the node — this matches which recursive traversal order? Answer with the traversal name.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about the COPY and EQUAL algorithms are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: COPY allocates a new node for every node in the original

feedback.text: Yes — a true copy creates fresh nodes.

answer.text: EQUAL returns true only when structure and values both match

feedback.text: Yes — both must agree.

answer.text: EQUAL of two empty trees returns not equal

feedback.text: No — two empty trees are equal.

answer.text: COPY runs in O(log n) time

feedback.text: No — COPY is O(n); every node is cloned.

generalfeedback.text: Both are O(n) recursive algorithms; COPY clones each node, and EQUAL demands matching structure and values, with both-empty ⇒ equal.
